compiled_state.title: As a contributor, my locally-authored tickets land in Jira with the right assignee or unassigned with an alert via BRIDGE_USER_MAP and two-step null-assignee
compiled_state.author: Test
compiled_state.description:
## Description

**What**: Implement BRIDGE_USER_MAP repo variable JSON lookup with case-insensitive email keys; on no-match, emit BRIDGE_ALERT and use a two-step pattern (POST create then PUT /rest/api/3/issue/{key}/assignee with accountId null) to explicitly unassign. Add a new AcliClient.unassign_issue(jira_key) method (existing _direct_rest_put wraps {"value": data} and is wrong shape for the assignee endpoint).

**Why**: Jira REST v3 deprecated displayName-based assign in 2019 (accountId only). ticket-lib-api.sh defaults assignee to git config user.name (Test/Worktree/Claude in worktree sessions). Current acli-integration.py retries-without-assignee silently with no user-map mechanism (verified zero matches). Research confirms accountId null via PUT /assignee is the de-facto convention (pycontribs/jira and atlassian-python-api both hardcode this); the -1 sentinel has documented bug JRACLOUD-71153.

**Scope**:
- IN: BRIDGE_USER_MAP env-var-driven JSON map read in bridge/_outbound_handlers.py and acli-integration.py, case-insensitive email lookup, AcliClient.unassign_issue() method, BRIDGE_ALERT on no-match, empirical verification of ACLI null-assignee wire format (HTTP-trace) OR direct REST v3 fallback path.
- OUT: dso-config.conf bridge.user_map.* keys (rejected per codebase-alignment finding — bridge scripts read os.environ exclusively), default-assignee config key (rejected by user during brainstorm).

## Done Definitions

- When this story is complete, BRIDGE_USER_MAP is read as a JSON object via os.environ.get("BRIDGE_USER_MAP", "{}") matching the INBOUND_STATUS_MAPPING pattern, and a contributor whose git author email is mapped (case-insensitive) lands in Jira with the configured Jira accountId as assignee ← Satisfies: "Locally-authored tickets created by a contributor whose git author email is mapped in BRIDGE_USER_MAP (case-insensitive) land in Jira with the configured Jira accountId as assignee"
- When this story is complete, a contributor with no user-map entry produces a BRIDGE_ALERT (reason: "no BRIDGE_USER_MAP entry for <email>") AND the resulting Jira issue is explicitly unassigned via POST create + PUT /rest/api/3/issue/{key}/assignee with body {"accountId": null} — verified by integration test with mocked Jira endpoint asserting the wire format ← Satisfies: "Locally-authored tickets with no user-map entry produce a BRIDGE_ALERT and arrive in Jira explicitly unassigned via a two-step pattern (POST create then PUT /rest/api/3/issue/{key}/assignee with accountId null)"
- When this story is complete, BRIDGE_USER_MAP key present but value empty string is treated as a no-match (BRIDGE_ALERT path) — NOT silently sent as accountId="" — verified by unit test ← Satisfies: SC4 (clarification of edge case)
- When this story is complete, AcliClient.unassign_issue(jira_key) method exists, posts {"accountId": null} as the body root (NOT wrapped in {"value": data}), and is unit-tested with a mock HTTP transport asserting the wire format ← Satisfies: SC4
- When this story is complete, the ACLI null-assignee wire format has been empirically verified — either by capturing an HTTP trace of acli's actual emission (cite the trace in the story note) or by implementing a direct REST v3 fallback via AcliClient session that bypasses acli for the unassign step (document which path was chosen in the story note) ← Satisfies: scrutiny consideration on closed-source binary verification
- When this story is complete, unit tests cover (a) email match exact case, (b) email match different case, (c) email not in map, (d) BRIDGE_USER_MAP unset (treat as empty map), (e) BRIDGE_USER_MAP malformed JSON (fail-open: treat as empty + warn), (f) value empty string ← Satisfies: TDD DoD for code-change story

## Considerations

- [Reliability] BRIDGE_USER_MAP must NOT be required — when unset, every contributor falls through to the BRIDGE_ALERT + unassigned path, NOT a hard fail. The hard fail is reserved for BRIDGE_ENV_ID (S2).
- [Codebase-alignment] Use os.environ.get pattern matching INBOUND_STATUS_MAPPING / INBOUND_TYPE_MAPPING; do NOT add a config reader for dso-config.conf (rejected per Plan-Review finding).
- [Testing] The two-step pattern unit test must assert both the POST body and the PUT body wire formats independently — verifying the issue creates first AND the unassign happens second.

## Escalation Policy

**Escalation policy**: Proceed unless a significant assumption is required to continue — one that could send the implementation in the wrong direction. Escalate only when genuinely blocked without a reasonable inference. Document all assumptions made without escalating.
